options.B: Take strong laxatives every evening to empty your bowels completely

question: What is one of the best long-term ways to improve maternal health in developing countries?

question: What is the main reason a doctor performs a joint arthroscopy?

question: Why do we love early detection of health issues during antenatal visits?

question: What is the main duty of the anaesthetist during an operation?

question: A healthy pregnant patient in her third trimester complains of feeling slightly short of breath during normal daily tasks. What is the best initial nursing interpretation?

question: Why is the blood-testis barrier (made by Sertoli cells) so important?

question: Which hormone helps your body handle long-term stress?

question: A nurse notices women suffering from regular coughs and eye irritation because they cook daily with firewood in closed kitchens. What is the main culprit here?

question: Why is timely documentation of assessment findings important for patient care?

question: A patient recovering from near-asphyxiation is cleared to eat, but struggles to swallow properly. Who should you consult?

question: What is the main role of the thalamus when processing sensory information?

question: Why are compression bands sometimes placed on the patient's abdomen during an IVP?

options.A: To push the contrast dye through the bloodstream much faster
options.B: To prevent the patient from moving around on the hard x-ray table
options.C: To keep the intravenous needle securely taped inside the vein
options.D: To slow urine flow and keep the upper renal system filled with dye

explanation: Abdominal compression temporarily traps the contrast in the kidneys and ureters, making those structures easier to see on the x-ray films. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T3#GNS213_U4_T3_h5)

question: A nurse is caring for a patient admitted with a highly contagious airborne respiratory infection. Which precaution is NOT appropriate for this specific case?

options.A: Housing the patient inside a negative pressure isolation room
options.B: Placing the patient in a standard open ward bed with no barriers
options.C: Ensuring healthcare workers wear fitted N95 respirator masks
options.D: Limiting visitor access to protect other vulnerable patients

explanation: Airborne infections require negative pressure rooms and specialized masks, not open wards where droplet nuclei can easily infect others. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T5#GNS123_U4_T5_h7)

question: Which health history complaint needs an urgent neurological check right away?

options.A: Occasional muscle cramps after heavy exercise
options.B: Sudden changes in speech and vision
options.C: Temporary skin dryness in cold weather
options.D: Mild fatigue after a full night of sleep

explanation: Sudden trouble talking or seeing are major warning signs for a stroke or another urgent brain emergency. Always stay alert for these! [learn more](GNS222_U3_T2#GNS222_U3_T2_h2)

question: Which disease is most commonly caught through accidental needle stick injuries in the clinic?

options.A: Malaria
options.B: Cholera
options.C: Typhoid fever
options.D: Hepatitis B

explanation: Hepatitis B is very easily spread through contaminated sharps in the hospital. This is why safety with needles is a huge deal for every nurse! [learn more](GNS122_U3_T7#GNS122_U3_T7_h2)

question: How does oxygen primarily travel through the bloodstream to body tissues?

options.A: Attached directly to white blood cells
options.B: Floating freely as pure gas bubbles in plasma
options.C: Bound to hemoglobin in red blood cells
options.D: Dissolved completely in blood platelets

explanation: The vast majority of oxygen in the body is carried by binding to the hemoglobin molecules inside red blood cells. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T6#GNS212_U4_T6_h2)

question: Which quick clinical bedside test is commonly used to check a patient's balance and stability?

options.A: Weber tuning fork test
options.B: Snellen chart test
options.C: Romberg test
options.D: Otoscopic examination

explanation: The Romberg test is a classic! You ask the patient to stand with their feet together and eyes closed to see how well their body maintains balance. [learn more](GNS311_U3_T8#GNS311_U3_T8_h2)

question: Which physical sign strongly points toward a uterine perforation or pelvic peritonitis?

options.A: Painless bilateral swelling of the lower extremities
options.B: Generalized skin rash and localized itching
options.C: Elevated blood pressure and clear breath sounds
options.D: A rigid and tender abdomen with rebound tenderness

explanation: When the lining of the belly (peritoneum) gets irritated or infected, the abdominal muscles lock up tight ('rigidity'), and pressing and letting go hurts sharply ('rebound tenderness'). A classic exam and ward clue! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T002#GNS226_U5_T002_h3)

question: A toddler with a throat infection starts making a harsh, high-pitched breathing sound (stridor) and flaring their nose. What should you do right away?

options.A: Encourage the child to eat a large solid meal
options.B: Notify the healthcare provider and prepare for airway support
options.C: Discharge the child home with instructions to rest
options.D: Apply a tight nasal pack to stop the secretions

explanation: Great clinical judgment! Stridor and nasal flaring mean the airway is struggling or narrowing. Call the doctor immediately and get ready to help the child breathe. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T3#GNS213_U2_T3_h6)

question: What is the primary goal of aseptic technique in nursing practice?

options.A: Eliminating all water in the room
options.B: Speeding up the patient discharge process
options.C: Minimizing pathogen contamination
options.D: Reducing the cost of hospital stays

explanation: Aseptic techniques are specifically designed practices that keep patients free from harmful disease-causing microbes during care. [learn more](GNS311_U4_T1#GNS311_U4_T1_h1)

question: What is the main reason nurses use fluorescein sodium eye drops?

options.A: To dilate the pupil for a deep retinal view
options.B: To kill bacteria causing severe pink eye
options.C: To highlight scratches and foreign objects on the cornea under special light
options.D: To numb the surface before checking eye pressure

explanation: Fluorescein is a brilliant diagnostic tool! It clings to damaged spots on the cornea and glows bright green under a blue light so you can easily spot tiny scratches. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T4#GNS215_U6_T4_h5)

question: Which mineral deficiency is particularly common in mountainous regions and areas far from the sea?

options.A: Calcium
options.B: Sodium
options.C: Vitamin C
options.D: Iodine

explanation: Iodine is naturally abundant in oceans and coastal soils, leaving inland and high-altitude regions vulnerable to low dietary intake. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T022#GNS227_U2_T022_h3)

question: Where is the favorite spot for patients to self-inject insulin regularly?

options.A: The chest wall over the sternum
options.B: The abdomen, avoiding the navel area
options.C: The anterior lower leg near the shin
options.D: The inner surface of the forearm

explanation: The tummy is easy to reach and has a nice, reliable layer of fat that absorbs insulin smoothly. Just remember to stay clear of the belly button! [learn more](GNS125_U3_T7#GNS125_U3_T7_h4)

question: How does placenta percreta differ from a simple placenta accreta?

options.A: Accreta occurs in the first trimester, while percreta occurs only at term.
options.B: Accreta involves the urinary bladder, while percreta stays inside the uterine cavity.
options.C: Percreta affects only the fetal membranes, while accreta affects the umbilical cord.
options.D: Percreta penetrates through the entire uterine wall, while accreta attaches only to the surface of the muscle.

explanation: Think of 'percreta' as breaking completely *through* the wall of the uterus, sometimes even touching nearby organs like the bladder. It's the most severe form! [learn more](GNS121_U6_T6#GNS121_U6_T6_h4)

question: What is the biggest risk of waiting too long to report a sudden drop in a patient's neuro status?

options.A: It increases the financial cost of hospital room supplies
options.B: It causes the nursing documentation to look untidy
options.C: It can delay life-saving interventions for acute brain injury
options.D: It forces the patient to stay in the hospital an extra day

explanation: Brain emergencies move fast! Reporting changes immediately can be the difference between a full recovery and permanent damage. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T2#GNS222_U3_T2_h9)

question: What is the main use of a fetal fibronectin test in the hospital?

options.A: To rule out delivery within the next two weeks when negative
options.B: To measure the precise level of maternal blood glucose
options.C: To confirm the exact gestational age in weeks and days
options.D: To detect active bacterial infections inside the bladder

explanation: A negative fetal fibronectin test is reassuring! It's like a reliable green light telling us delivery isn't happening in the next 14 days. Brilliant clinical knowledge! [learn more](GNS226_U4_T001#GNS226_U4_T001_h4)

question: A patient tells you they drink alcohol 'only socially.' What is your best next step?

options.A: Accept the vague answer and move on to the next topic
options.B: Document that the patient denies all alcohol consumption
options.C: Assume the patient is hiding a severe addiction disorder
options.D: Ask specifically how many drinks they consume per week

explanation: Great thinking! 'Socially' means different things to everyone, so getting a specific number helps you understand their actual intake. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T3#GNS222_U3_T3_h5)

question: What is the main difference between structural heart disorders and electrical heart problems?

options.A: Structural disorders involve physical defects in heart valves, walls, or muscle.
options.B: Structural disorders can never be present at birth.
options.C: Electrical problems always require open-heart surgery.
options.D: Electrical problems only affect the right side of the heart.

explanation: Think of structural heart issues as physical problems with the heart's building blocks (like valves or walls), while electrical problems mess up the heart's natural wiring and rhythm. You've got this! [learn more](GNS213_U1_T5#GNS213_U1_T5_h1)

question: In family planning clinics, how do we define a 'new acceptor'?

options.A: A nurse newly transferred to manage the reproductive health unit
options.B: A patient returning to the clinic for a routine resupply visit
options.C: A client adopting a modern contraceptive method for the first time
options.D: A community leader who just agreed to support safe motherhood

explanation: Spot on! A new acceptor is simply someone starting modern contraception for the very first time in their life. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T028#GNS226_U6_T028_h3)

question: A patient has a stubborn, hard mass of stool that normal enemas can't shift. What procedure is best here?

options.A: A rectal washout
options.B: An intravenous fluid bolus
options.C: A nasogastric tube insertion
options.D: An oral laxative challenge

explanation: When standard enemas aren't strong enough to break up severe blockages, a rectal washout provides the extra mechanical help needed. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T13#GNS212_U1_T13_h2)

question: What is the correct sequence of the three stages in the General Adaptation Syndrome (GAS)?

options.A: Alarm reaction, exhaustion, resistance
options.B: Alarm reaction, resistance, exhaustion
options.C: Resistance, exhaustion, alarm reaction
options.D: Exhaustion, alarm reaction, resistance

explanation: Easy to remember: First you sound the Alarm, then you Try to resist it, and if it won't stop, your body reaches Exhaustion. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T6#GNS313_U3_T6_h3)

question: Why are infectious agents like Hepatitis B classified as cancer risk factors?

options.A: They immediately destroy all red blood cells in the body
options.B: They lower body temperature and stop normal digestion
options.C: They block the absorption of vital nutrients in the gut
options.D: They cause chronic inflammation and cellular damage over time

explanation: Certain viruses and bacteria lead to long-term tissue damage and inflammation, which increases the chance of cellular mutations. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T1#GNS321_U1_T1_h4)

question: Why do fast-growing malignant tumors encourage angiogenesis (the growth of new blood vessels)?

options.A: It causes the tumor cells to mature and look normal
options.B: It stops the tumor from spreading to other organs
options.C: It helps cancer cells hide from white blood cells
options.D: It creates new blood vessels to supply oxygen and nutrients

explanation: Clever! Tumors need food and oxygen to keep growing rapidly. By triggering angiogenesis, they force the body to build a dedicated supply line straight to them. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T6#GNS321_U1_T6_h3)

question: A patient taking high-dose prednisone for six months reports feeling very hungry all the time and notices weight gain around the face and neck. What causes this?

options.A: Fluid is building up inside the brain tissue.
options.B: Steroids alter how the body stores fat and stimulates appetite.
options.C: The medication is destroying the thyroid gland completely.
options.D: The patient is secretly eating too much junk food at night.

explanation: Corticosteroids alter carbohydrate and fat metabolism, frequently causing increased appetite and fat redistribution. [learn more](GNS223_U5_T3#GNS223_U5_T3_h5)

question: Which virus is directly linked to causing Kaposi sarcoma?

options.A: Human papillomavirus
options.B: Epstein-Barr virus
options.C: Human herpesvirus 8
options.D: Cytomegalovirus

explanation: Kaposi sarcoma develops due to a coinfection with human herpesvirus 8 when the immune system is too weak to fight it off. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T13#GNS216_U6_T13_h3)

question: What is a major benefit of community genetic counseling for inherited blood disorders?

options.A: Manufacturing safe blood products for local hospital use
options.B: Providing free meals for patients with severe chronic anemia
options.C: Helping families understand their risk of passing conditions to children
options.D: Treating acute bleeding episodes in emergency rooms

explanation: Genetic counseling educates couples about their carrier status and the statistical chances of having children with conditions like sickle cell anemia. [learn more](GNS311_U2_T15#GNS311_U2_T15_h7)

question: How should an accountable leader react when a serious clinical error happens on their ward?

options.A: Pretend the event never happened to protect the hospital's image
options.B: Hide the incident report so no one else finds out about it
options.C: Punish the entire nursing shift immediately without investigating
options.D: Use the mistake as an opportunity for systemic review and learning

explanation: Blaming people doesn't stop future errors. Accountable leaders look at the bigger picture to see what in the system failed, turning mistakes into valuable lessons. [learn more](GST321_U3_T4#GST321_U3_T4_h7)

question: Why do new mothers need scheduled postnatal check-ups?

options.A: It is primarily required to register the baby's birth certificate
options.B: It helps detect early complications and supports maternal recovery
options.C: It guarantees that the mother will not experience postpartum depression
options.D: It replaces the need for childhood immunizations

explanation: Great thinking! These visits let us keep an eye on physical healing, encourage breastfeeding, and catch any sneaky complications early before they become serious. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T021#GNS226_U3_T021_h1)

question: Why does a client with untreated diabetes experience frequent urination?

options.A: The kidneys enlarge to remove excess protein from the bloodstream
options.B: Excess glucose pulls water into the urine through osmotic diuresis
options.C: Infections destroy the sphincter muscles that control urine release
options.D: High blood sugar directly irritates the lining of the urinary bladder

explanation: When sugar spills into the urine, it acts like a sponge, drawing extra water along with it and causing high urine output. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T8#GNS222_U2_T8_h4)

question: Why must nurses consider a patient's cultural and socioeconomic background when planning a diet?

options.A: Culture dictates the exact BMR of every individual person
options.B: Religious practices completely eliminate the need for vitamins
options.C: Socioeconomic status determines how fast the stomach digests fats
options.D: These factors heavily influence food availability and traditional choices

explanation: Dietary habits are deeply tied to culture, beliefs, and economic access, which nurses must respect to ensure compliance. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T015#GNS227_U2_T015_h7)

question: Which neurotransmitter works to calm down electrical activity in the brain and balance things out?

options.A: GABA
options.B: Glutamate
options.C: Epinephrine
options.D: Dopamine

explanation: GABA is the brain's main 'braking' system. It helps calm down nerve activity so things don't get too excited. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T19#GNS222_U3_T19_h5)

question: Why should nurses look at patient-reported outcomes alongside lab test results in endocrine care?

options.A: Lab numbers alone do not capture the patient's daily quality of life
options.B: Lab results are legally required to be ignored if the patient feels fine
options.C: Patients always understand laboratory science better than doctors
options.D: Patient feelings are the only accurate diagnostic tool available

explanation: Spot on! Good labs are important, but understanding how the patient actually feels and lives day-to-day is what truly matters in nursing. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T17#GNS222_U2_T17_h7)

question: A client taking daily ibuprofen for knee osteoarthritis tells the nurse they noticed dark, tarry stools. What is the nurse's best action?

options.A: Tell the client to drink more water and double their daily walking distance
options.B: Suggest that the client switch to taking the pain pill on an empty stomach
options.C: Instruct the client to stop the ibuprofen and report the finding to the provider immediately
options.D: Explain that dark stools are a normal side effect of all joint medications

explanation: Dark, tarry stools indicate upper gastrointestinal bleeding, a serious complication of NSAID use that requires immediate medical attention. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T14#GNS222_U1_T14_h8)

question: Your patient's GCS score keeps dropping over the last two hours. What should this trend tell you immediately?

options.A: Normal tiredness at the end of the day
options.B: A minor hearing loss developing in the patient
options.C: Worsening neurological status and potential brain swelling
options.D: A temporary reaction to hospital food

explanation: A falling GCS score is a serious warning sign. It means brain function is declining and you must act fast! [learn more](GNS222_U3_T4#GNS222_U3_T4_h7)

question: Which laboratory test is used to definitively diagnose sickle cell anaemia?

options.A: Erythrocyte sedimentation rate
options.B: Coagulation profile test
options.C: Complete blood count
options.D: Haemoglobin electrophoresis

explanation: Haemoglobin electrophoresis is the gold standard test! It separates different types of haemoglobin in a sample so the lab can clearly spot abnormal haemoglobin S. [learn more](GNS311_U2_T7#GNS311_U2_T7_h3)

question: Which of these is a classic long-term heart problem tied to heavy, chronic drinking?

options.A: Permanent stabilization of heart valves
options.B: Cardiomyopathy and hypertension
options.C: Significantly lowered resting pulse rate
options.D: Increased production of red blood cells

explanation: Over time, heavy drinking weakens the heart muscle (cardiomyopathy) and drives up blood pressure (hypertension). Take care of that ticker! [learn more](GNS227_U4_T013#GNS227_U4_T013_h4)

question: Why do we grab a cold pack immediately after someone suffers a fresh joint sprain?

options.A: To heat up the deep tissue and relax tight tendons
options.B: To stimulate rapid cell division in the bone
options.C: To dilate vessels and increase local bleeding
options.D: To constrict blood vessels and reduce swelling

explanation: Spot on! Cold causes vasoconstriction (narrowing the vessels), which slows down blood flow to the fresh injury so it doesn't blow up into a huge swelling. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T8#GNS221_U3_T8_h2)

question: Which hormone does the hypothalamus release in pulses to wake up the pituitary gland?

options.A: Progesterone
options.B: Luteinizing Hormone
options.C: Gonadotropin-Releasing Hormone
options.D: Follicle-Stimulating Hormone

explanation: Think of the hypothalamus as the master controller. It sends out Gonadotropin-Releasing Hormone (GnRH) as a messenger signal to get the pituitary gland to join the action! [learn more](GNS216_U2_T5#GNS216_U2_T5_h2)

question: What pocket of pus can develop near the fallopian tube and ovary during a bad pelvic infection?

options.A: Cervical retention nodule
options.B: Endometrial polyp
options.C: Uterine fibroid cyst
options.D: Tubo-ovarian abscess

explanation: When upper reproductive infections get severe, pus can collect and form a painful pocket involving both the tube and the ovary, called a tubo-ovarian abscess. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T30#GNS216_U5_T30_h3)

question: Which blood test checks how well the liver is making proteins needed for blood clotting?

options.A: Prothrombin time (PT/INR)
options.B: Direct bilirubin level
options.C: Serum creatinine
options.D: Alanine aminotransferase (ALT)

explanation: Spot on! Because the liver builds most of our clotting factors, testing how long blood takes to clot (PT/INR) shows us how well the liver is working. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T5#GNS222_U2_T5_h5)

question: Why do patients with chronic renal failure frequently look very pale and complain of severe tiredness?

options.A: The liver stops producing enough protein to carry vitamins.
options.B: Decreased erythropoietin production leads to anemia.
options.C: Excess sodium in the blood blocks oxygen from entering the lungs.
options.D: High potassium levels destroy red blood cells in the bloodstream.

explanation: Remember, damaged kidneys forget to make enough erythropoietin—the hormone that tells your bone marrow to build red blood cells. Without it, anemia sets in! [learn more](GNS213_U4_T7#GNS213_U4_T7_h3)

question: When should standard precautions be used in clinical practice?

options.A: Only when blood or body fluid is visibly staining the bedsheets
options.B: To every patient, regardless of their diagnosis or infection status
options.C: Strictly during surgical procedures in the main operating theatre
options.D: Only when caring for patients with known infectious diseases

explanation: Treat every patient as potentially infectious. Standard precautions keep you and everyone around you safe from hidden germs. [learn more](GNS122_U3_T7#GNS122_U3_T7_h7)

question: When is a closed-ended question most helpful during an assessment?

options.A: When starting the orientation phase of an admission
options.B: When you need a quick, specific fact like a drug allergy
options.C: When you want the patient to describe their life story
options.D: When the patient is feeling anxious and needs to vent

explanation: Correct! Closed questions are great when you just need quick, straight-to-the-point facts like dates, numbers, or allergies. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T3#GNS112_U3_T3_h4)

question: Which detail is essential to include when charting after suctioning a patient?

options.A: Color, consistency, and amount of the removed secretions
options.B: The exact brand name of the sterile gloves used
options.C: The name of the company that manufactured the suction machine
options.D: The room temperature at the moment of the procedure

explanation: Recording the characteristics of mucus gives vital clues about infection, hydration status, and overall lung health. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T12#GNS212_U2_T12_h7)

question: Why are babies born to unvaccinated mothers at such high risk for tetanus?

options.A: They are more susceptible to common household bacteria
options.B: They lack protective antibodies passed from the mother
options.C: Their umbilical cords take much longer to heal naturally
options.D: They fail to absorb nutrients from breast milk properly

explanation: You got it! When a mother is vaccinated during pregnancy, she passes protective antibodies to her baby to shield them until they can make their own. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T018#GNS226_U3_T018_h3)

question: What is the main job of an enteric coating on a tablet?

options.A: To allow the nurse to crush the pill easily into food
options.B: To help the tablet dissolve much faster in the mouth
options.C: To make the pill taste sweet for children
options.D: To protect the stomach lining and prevent acid breakdown

explanation: Think of an enteric coating as a special shield! It helps the pill ignore harsh stomach acid so it can safely reach the small intestine before dissolving. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T4#GNS125_U3_T4_h2)

question: Why is a severe bleeding disorder a major concern before arthrocentesis?

options.A: It completely prevents the lab from analyzing the sample
options.B: It can cause dangerous bleeding inside the joint space
options.C: It stops the local anesthetic from numbing the skin
options.D: It makes the synovial fluid too thick to withdraw

explanation: Poor clotting function puts the patient at risk of bleeding into the closed joint cavity, leading to painful hemarthrosis. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T8#GNS222_U1_T8_h3)

question: An elderly patient refuses to eat the standard hospital diet because it feels strange to them. What is the best holistic nursing action?

options.A: Report the patient to the medical director for being uncooperative
options.B: Collaborate with the patient to include familiar, culturally accepted local foods
options.C: Force-feed the patient to ensure they meet their daily caloric requirements
options.D: Discharge the patient immediately for refusing hospital dietary guidelines

explanation: Spot on! Holistic care respects cultural preferences and partners with the patient to find workable, comforting dietary solutions. [learn more](GNS123_U1_T2#GNS123_U1_T2_h6)

question: Why should a nurse use a tongue depressor or gloved finger rather than bare fingers to scoop cream from a jar?

options.A: To force the cream to bypass the epidermal stratum corneum layer
options.B: To ensure the cream is heated to body temperature before spreading
options.C: To make the medication absorb five times faster into the bloodstream
options.D: To prevent contaminating the entire container of medication with microbes

explanation: Dipping bare hands into a shared medication jar introduces bacteria from the nurse's hands into the product, risking infection for future applications. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T16#GNS125_U3_T16_h7)

question: Which hormone is most strongly linked to the severe nausea of early pregnancy?

options.A: Prolactin
options.B: Insulin
options.C: Oxytocin
options.D: Human chorionic gonadotropin

explanation: Rapidly rising levels of human chorionic gonadotropin peak in the first trimester and strongly correlate with intense nausea and vomiting. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T016#GNS226_U2_T016_h2)

question: Why did Florence Nightingale place the most severely injured soldiers closest to the nurse's station?

options.A: To make it easier for doctors to perform sudden surgeries
options.B: To keep them away from noisy convalescing soldiers
options.C: To comply with strict military hierarchy rules
options.D: To allow for closer and more frequent observation

explanation: Placing the sickest patients near the nurses allowed staff to detect rapid changes in condition early. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T1#GNS321_U2_T1_h1)

question: When does everyday worry cross the line into a clinical anxiety disorder?

options.A: Normal worry only occurs in children and teenagers.
options.B: Normal worry never causes physical symptoms like a racing heart.
options.C: Clinical anxiety persists excessively and disrupts daily functioning.
options.D: Clinical anxiety disappears immediately once a stressor is removed.

explanation: We all worry about exams or finances sometimes! But clinical anxiety hangs around stubbornly and makes it hard to get through daily life. Spotting this difference helps you understand when a patient truly needs support. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T10#GNS123_U3_T10_h1)

question: Why is early initiation of CPR critical during a cardiac arrest?

options.A: It prevents permanent brain damage by maintaining minimal perfusion
options.B: It eliminates the need for any medications or defibrillation later
options.C: It completely cures the underlying heart disease causing the arrest
options.D: It guarantees the immediate return of spontaneous heartbeat

explanation: Brain cells begin to die within minutes without oxygen, so starting compressions quickly buys vital time. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T1#GNS212_U2_T1_h1)

question: Why might a nurse not see all three signs of Beck's triad in every patient with cardiac tamponade?

options.A: Intravenous fluids always hide these specific physical signs.
options.B: Beck's triad only occurs during blunt trauma, never penetrating trauma.
options.C: The triad only appears after the patient has fully recovered.
options.D: The classic signs do not show up in every single patient.

explanation: Textbook signs are great to learn, but real patients don't always read the textbook! Clinical signs vary depending on how fast the bleeding happens. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T9#GNS213_U1_T9_h4)

question: A nurse places a naked newborn directly onto a cold metal scale. What type of heat loss is this?

options.A: Evaporation
options.B: Radiation
options.C: Convection
options.D: Conduction

explanation: Conduction happens when the baby touches a cooler surface directly, like a cold scale. That's why we always put a warm towel down first in the ward! [learn more](GNS226_U3_T014#GNS226_U3_T014_h2)

question: An admission that is planned well in advance for a scheduled surgical procedure is called what?

options.A: An elective admission
options.B: An emergency admission
options.C: A transfer admission
options.D: An acute admission

explanation: Elective admissions are scheduled ahead of time because the patient's condition is stable enough to wait for a convenient date. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T5#GNS112_U2_T5_h2)

question: Why is losing a pulse considered a very late and dangerous sign of compartment syndrome?

options.A: Arteries have thick walls and are the last vessels to collapse under pressure.
options.B: Pulse checks are unreliable unless done with a special electronic machine.
options.C: Blood flow actually increases in the early stages of compartment pressure.
options.D: Nerves stop working before blood vessels even begin to narrow.

explanation: Major arteries are tough and hold out the longest. Nerves and tiny capillaries get crushed and starved of oxygen way before the main pulse disappears. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T23#GNS222_U1_T23_h4)

question: Why are patients advised not to smoke on the morning of their barium swallow test?

options.A: Smoking causes immediate closure of the upper esophageal sphincter
options.B: Smoking increases stomach acid and swallowing secretions
options.C: Nicotine dissolves the barium contrast inside the mouth
options.D: The X-ray machine reacts poorly with tobacco smoke in the room

explanation: Nicotine stimulates gastric activity and excess saliva or acid production, which can interfere with clear imaging of the upper GI tract. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T13#GNS221_U2_T13_h3)

question: When is ECMO (Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation) usually considered for a COVID-19 patient?

options.A: Immediately upon admission before trying simple nasal cannula oxygen
options.B: As the first-line treatment for all patients with a mild cough
options.C: When the patient is ready to be weaned off all breathing support
options.D: When conventional mechanical ventilation fails to maintain adequate oxygen levels

question: A patient who tested positive for a late-onset degenerative disorder expresses severe anxiety about the future and refuses to talk to family. What is the most appropriate nursing action?

options.C: Tell the patient not to worry because symptoms might never appear

question: A patient is admitted with active pulmonary tuberculosis. Which specific protective gear must the nurse wear before entering the room?

question: Why is calling anticoagulants 'blood thinners' a bit misleading?

options.C: They only affect plasma proteins and leave red blood cells alone

question: Why should the fluid bag be kept at a low height during a washout?

question: How does the progestin in injectable contraceptives mainly stop sperm from reaching an egg?

question: Tracking a patient's fluid intake and output mainly helps you evaluate what?

question: Why should nurses participate in emotional debriefing after handling multiple patient deaths?

question: What actually causes that sharp, terrible pain and swelling during a gout flare?

question: What happens to a mother's insulin requirements immediately after the placenta is delivered?

question: Why is it best for nurses to avoid giving false reassurance like 'everything will be fine'?
